key_takeaways: British couples who live in the UK can marry legally in Greece. The legal steps run through the Greek municipality where you marry, and Chania and Heraklion publish document lists for foreigners who do not live in Greece.

Your proof that you are free to marry comes from the FCDO through the gov.uk online service. The FCDO fee for a certificate of no impediment or a local equivalent is GBP 50 per document, and the Greece-specific details show only inside the application.

UK birth certificates need a paper apostille from the FCDO Legalisation Office (GBP 45 per document plus postage, usually up to 25 working days plus delivery), then a Greek translation from a translator on the Greek Foreign Ministry's register.

A 4 January 2019 Greek Interior Ministry circular indicates that a foreign free-to-marry document naming your partner counts as the Greek licence, so ask your municipality in writing whether it accepts yours before you pay non-refundable deposits.

gov.uk says a marriage abroad is recognised in the UK if it was lawful where it took place and would be allowed under UK law. It is not registered in the UK, so your Greek certificate is your proof, including for a passport in your married name.

faq.q: How do UK couples get married in Greece?
faq.a: You apply through gov.uk for the FCDO document that shows you are free to marry, have your birth certificate apostilled by the FCDO Legalisation Office, and have both translated into Greek. You then lodge them with the municipality where you will marry, which sets the ceremony arrangements and holds the civil ceremony; ask it which documents, translations and dates apply to your own passports.

faq.q: Is a wedding in Greece legal in the UK?
faq.a: Yes, if it was lawful in Greece and would be allowed under UK law, according to gov.uk. It is not registered in the UK, so keep your Greek certificate safe.

faq.q: Do British citizens need a certificate of no impediment to marry in Greece?
faq.a: You need a document proving you are free to marry; gov.uk's online service shows whether that is a certificate of no impediment or another document. Chania also wants it to name your partner.

faq.q: How long do we need to be in Greece before the wedding?
faq.a: Your municipality decides. The one-week wait belongs to the residents' licence and is not on Chania's or Heraklion's non-resident lists, so ask how many working days the town hall needs your originals.

faq.q: Is it different if we live in Scotland or Northern Ireland?
faq.a: The FCDO and Greek steps are the same for every British passport holder, and gov.uk says only UK marriages and civil partnerships are registered in the UK. Check with the register office where your birth was registered which certificate to order for an apostille and, if you marry at home first, check with the register office where you will marry for its notice period and the documents it needs.
